title: How to Pray — The Essentials
subtitle: The five daily prayers, step by step from standing to salaam
steps: Niyyah (intention) — settle the heart on which prayer and how many rak'ahs; the Prophet ﷺ said: actions are judged by intentions (Bukhari 1). Intention is in the heart, not spoken aloud.
Face the qiblah, standing. Men raise hands to the ears (women to the shoulders) saying Allahu Akbar — the prayer has begun; everything before this was worldly (Bukhari 756).
Recite the opening supplication (thana'), then Ayat al-Kursi or another passage, then Surah al-Fatihah — the Prophet ﷺ said there is no prayer for the one who does not recite it (Bukhari 756).
Ruku' — bow with the back level, saying Subhana Rabbiyal-'Azim three times.
Stand from ruku' saying Sami'allahu liman hamidah... Rabbana wa lakal-hamd.
Sujud — prostrate on seven limbs: forehead (with nose), two hands, two knees, two feet — saying Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la three times (Bukhari 812).
Sit between the two prostrations, then prostrate again — that is one rak'ah. Repeat per the prayer: Fajr 2, Dhuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3, Isha 4.
In the final sitting: the tashahhud, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, and any dua; then the salaam: Assalamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah, turning right then left (Bukhari 831).
madhhabNote: Differences between the four schools (hand positions, recitation aloud vs silent, amin aloud) are all valid — the Huda rule: follow one school's fiqh completely, or ask a local teacher.

title: Wudu — The Purifying Wash
subtitle: How the Prophet ﷺ washed for prayer
steps: Niyyah in the heart, then Bismillah; the Prophet ﷺ said: there is no wudu for the one who does not mention Allah (Abu Dawud 101, hasan).
Wash the hands three times, right then left (Bukhari 159).
Rinse the mouth and nose three times with one handful (Bukhari 159).
Wash the face three times — from the hairline to the chin, ear to ear.
Wash the arms to the elbows, right then left, three times (Qur'an 5:6).
Wipe the head once — wet hands from the forehead to the nape and back (Qur'an 5:6), then the ears.
Wash the feet to the ankles three times, right then left — the Prophet ﷺ said: woe to the heels from the Fire (Bukhari 163).
The seal: the shahada — Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah... and the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him (Muslim 234).

title: Ghusl — The Full Purification
subtitle: After janabah, menstruation's end, and before Friday prayer (sunnah)
steps: Niyyah in the heart; begin Bismillah.
Wash the hands, then wash the private parts — the Prophet ﷺ used to do this first (Bukhari 248).
Perform a complete wudu as for prayer (Bukhari 248).
Pour water over the head three times, letting it reach the roots of the hair — even under a thick braid (the matted-haired woman, Muslim 330).
Wash the right side of the body, then the left — the water must touch every part, nothing dry (Bukhari 193).
Optional seal (sunnah): the Friday ghusl — the Prophet ﷺ commanded it and even used to wash every Friday, perfume, and wear his best (Bukhari 902).
madhhabNote: Order differs between schools (some wash the whole body first, wudu after) — all trace to the Prophet's ﷺ practice; follow your school's fiqh.

title: Tayammum — The Dry Purification
subtitle: When water is absent, harmful, or out of reach
steps: Condition: no water, or water would harm (illness, cold), or no access. The command: 'and if you are ill or on a journey... then seek clean earth' (Qur'an 4:43, 5:6).
Strike the clean earth (dust, sand, stone) once with both palms.
Wipe the face with them (Qur'an 4:43).
Strike the earth again — and wipe the hands and arms to the elbows (Qur'an 5:6).
Pray with it — it lifts every restriction water would lift; the earth was made for you as a purifier (Bukhari 335).
It expires with the finding of water: the Prophet ﷺ struck the earth and prayed, then water was brought and he did not repeat the prayer (Bukhari 344).

title: The Adhan & Iqamah
subtitle: The call that empties the unseen world of devils
steps: The mu'adhin faces the qiblah, raises the voice, and calls: Allahu Akbar (4x), Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah (2x), Ash-hadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah (2x), Hayya 'alas-salah (2x), Hayya 'alal-falah (2x), Allahu Akbar (2x), La ilaha illa Allah (Bukhari 604).
In Fajr, after Hayya 'alal-falah: As-salatu khayrun minan-nawm (2x) (Bukhari 589).
The effect: Shaytan hears the adhan and flees, passing wind until he cannot hear it (Bukhari 608).
Repeat after the mu'adhin, and after the last phrase send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ — your intercession becomes obligatory for him (Muslim 384).
Then ask: Allahumma rabba hadhihid-da'watit-tammah... — the Prophet ﷺ said whoever says it, my intercession for him becomes obligatory (Bukhari 589).
The iqamah: the same words as adhan, doubled phrases said once, ending with Qad qamatis-salat (2x) — prayed immediately after it (Abu Dawud 500).

title: Friday Prayer — The Essentials
subtitle: Jumu'ah: the weekly gathering with conditions and sunnahs
steps: Obligatory on every free, resident, adult Muslim man; women are exempt but rewarded for attending (Bukhari 876).
The ghusl before it is obligatory — the Prophet ﷺ commanded every accountable person to wash on Friday (Bukhari 877).
Wear the best clean clothes; early arrival is multiplied — the Prophet ﷺ compared the stages of arrival to sacrifices: as if a camel, then a cow, then a sheep... (Bukhari 881).
Listen in silence: even saying 'be quiet' to a talker during the khutbah forfeits the reward (Bukhari 892).
The prayer: two rak'ahs after the khutbah, led by the imam (Bukhari 883).
The missed window: Jumu'ah has a fixed hour when no Muslim asks Allah but He grants it — the Prophet ﷺ indicated it is between the imam sitting and the prayer's end (Bukhari 935).

title: Making Up Missed Prayers
subtitle: Qada' — the debt that only you can pay
steps: The duty: a missed obligatory prayer must be prayed — 'the Prophet ﷺ was asked about a man who slept through the prayer: he said: there is no negligence in sleep; negligence is only while awake' (Muslim 681).
Pray it as soon as remembered — 'when any of you forgets the prayer, let him pray it when he remembers' (Bukhari 597).
Order: keep the prayers in sequence when possible; if several prayers are owed and only part can be caught, begin with the earliest missed (the majority view).
Do not trade it for nawafil: 'there is no make-up for the one who delays beyond its time, and his excessive works are the expiation' (Muslim 684) — the missed prayer stands as a debt until paid.
Practical system: the Prophet ﷺ taught a habit for forgetfulness — say the isti'adhah and dhikr after prayer so forgetfulness becomes rare (Bukhari 1374).
Ask: if sleep, travel, or genuine forgetfulness caused the miss — pray it without blame; deliberate neglect is the danger, and its cure is repentance plus immediate qada.
madhhabNote: The schools differ on whether multiple missed prayers must be prayed in strict order (hanafi: yes, with cause for exception; shafi'i: recommended; hanbali: obligatory). Follow your school.

title: The Rawatib — Prayers Around the Obligatory
subtitle: The sunnah prayers that guard the fard
steps: Fajr: two sunnah rak'ahs — 'the two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than the world and everything in it' (Muslim 725).
Dhuhr: four before (and two after) — 'if anyone prays four before Dhuhr and four after, Allah forbids him the Fire' (Tirmidhi 428, hasan).
Maghrib: two after; Isha: two after.
The night prayer (qiyam): two by two — 'the night prayer is two by two, and witr is one rak'ah' (Bukhari 990).
Witr: the Prophet ﷺ never abandoned it, neither traveling nor resident (Bukhari 990).
Duha: the mid-morning prayer — 'a prayer of the repentant, prayed when the young camels feel the sun's heat' (Muslim 748).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 990; Sahih Muslim 725, 748; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 428

title: Mosque Manners
subtitle: The adab of the house of Allah
steps: Enter with the right foot and the dua: Bismillah, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala Rasulillah... (Bukhari 1131, abridged).
Pray the two rak'ahs of greeting (tahiyyat al-masjid) before sitting — 'when one of you enters the mosque, let him not sit until he prays two rak'ahs' (Bukhari 1163).
Keep the voice low: the Prophet ﷺ forbade raising voices in recitation in the mosque except at a level of self-reminder (Abu Dawud 1332).
Do not pass in front of a praying person — the hadith likens that to a donkey passing before an archer (Bukhari 509).
Leave with the left foot and the leaving-dua (inverse of the entering).
Photography, eating, and trade are for elsewhere: 'whoever eats garlic or onions, let him keep away from us — or from our mosque' (Bukhari 545).

title: Entering & Leaving the Home
subtitle: Bismillah at the door, gratitude at the threshold
steps: Enter with the right foot, saying Bismillah; the Prophet ﷺ named the entering-dua (Bismillah, was-salamu... ) — 'Shaytan then says to his companion: no lodging or supper for you tonight' (Muslim 2018).
Mention Allah over food and drink — 'mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest you' (Bukhari 5376).
Leave with the left foot and the leaving-dua: Bismillah, tawakkaltu 'alallah, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

The greeting inside: spread the salam — 'you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another; shall I guide you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the salam among you' (Muslim 54).

title: Washing the Deceased
subtitle: Ghusl al-mayyit — the final service, done gently
steps: The one who washes is trustworthy, bathes first, and covers the body; men wash men, women wash women — spouses may wash each other (Bukhari 1254).
The Prophet ﷺ said of the washer: 'wash her three times, or five, or seven — odd numbers — and begin with her right side and the places of wudu' (Bukhari 1253).
Camphor is used in the final wash — 'the best of your perfumes is camphor' (Bukhari 1242).
Comb the hair, wash gently; the Prophet ﷺ said: treat the deceased gently, for the believer is honored by Allah (Abu Dawud 3142).
The water used last is poured with the du'a for forgiveness — 'O Allah, forgive him, have mercy on him, pardon him...' (Muslim 916).

title: The Funeral Prayer
subtitle: Salat al-janazah — no ruku', no sujud, only dua
steps: Stand in rows facing the qiblah; the imam stands at the head of a man, the middle of a woman (Bukhari 1331).
Four takbirs: Allahu Akbar, then the opening supplication (al-Thanaiya); Allahu Akbar, then blessings on the Prophet ﷺ; Allahu Akbar, then the dua for the deceased (Muslim 916).
The dua: Allahumma-ghfir lahu, warhamhu, wa 'afihi, wa'fu 'anhu... — the Prophet ﷺ taught it, and for a woman, the endings change (Bukhari 1334).
A fourth takbir, then one may add a personal dua; the salam follows — one salam to the right (most schools).

The reward: 'whoever follows a funeral and prays over it, he earns a qirat; and whoever stays until the burial, two qirats' — the companions asked: what are two qirats? He said: like two great mountains (Bukhari 1325).

title: The Burial & Visiting Graves
subtitle: Hasten the burial; visit to remember, not to worship
steps: Hasten it: 'hasten with the deceased, for if it was righteous, you are forwarding it to good; and if otherwise, you are taking a burden off your necks' (Bukhari 1315).
The grave: dug as a lahd (niche) where the ground allows; the body laid on its right side facing the qiblah.
The earth is thrown — three handfuls from the head's end, with: minha khalaqnakum... (Bukhari 1337).
No wailing, no fire-brands of grief, no bare heads from grief itself — 'the deceased is punished by the wailing of his family' (Bukhari 1296).
Visiting graves: the Prophet ﷺ permitted it — 'I had forbidden you to visit graves, but now visit them, for they remind you of the Hereafter' (Muslim 977).
The greeting of the grave: Assalamu 'alaykum ahlal-qubur... (Muslim 977).

title: Consoling the Bereaved
subtitle: What to say when there is nothing to say
steps: The sunnah phrase: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un; Allahumma-jurni fi musibati, wakhluf li khayran minha — 'O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with better' (Muslim 2123).
Say what eases: the Prophet ﷺ said: 'whoever consoles a bereaved person has a garment of honor upon him on the Day of Resurrection' (Tirmidhi 1075).
Do not say 'it could be worse' or 'be strong' — the sunnah is to speak the phrases of tawhid and reward.
Serve the family: bring food — 'the family of Ja'far are preoccupied; feed them' (Abu Dawud 3128).
The three-day gathering limit: it is for the relatives to prepare food for the bereaved, not the reverse (Bukhari 1340).
Pray for the dead in their absence: 'the prayer of the absent reaches' (Baihaqi, hasan).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1340; Sahih Muslim 2123; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1075

title: Eating Manners
subtitle: One-third for food, one-third for drink, one-third for breath
steps: Say Bismillah; if forgotten: Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirahu (Abu Dawud 3767).
Eat with the right hand — 'the Shaytan eats with his left hand and drinks with his left' (Muslim 2020).
Eat from what is nearest — 'eat from what is nearest to you' (Bukhari 5376).
The portion: 'the son of Adam fills no vessel worse than his stomach — a few morsels suffice him; but if he must, then one-third for food, one-third for drink, one-third for breath' (Ibn Majah 3349).
Eat together — 'the food of one suffices two, and the food of two suffices four' (Bukhari 5392).
Praise after: Alhamdulillahil-ladhi at'amana... — 'Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a morsel and praises Him for it' (Muslim 2734).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 5376, 5392; Sahih Muslim 2020, 2734; Sunan Ibn Majah 3349

title: Sleeping Manners
subtitle: The night as worship's gateway
steps: Before bed: ayat al-Kursi — 'a guardian from Allah stays with you and no devil approaches you until morning' (Bukhari 2311).
The three quls: blow into the palms, wipe over what you can reach of the body (Bukhari 5017).
Sleep on the right side — 'when you go to bed, lie on your right side' (Bukhari 247).
The duas: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya; and on waking: Alhamdulillahil-ladhi ahyana... (Bukhari 6324).
Recitation before sleep: al-Mulk — 'there is a surah of thirty verses which intercedes for a man until he is forgiven: Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion' (Abu Dawud 1400).
The night is also for prayer: 'the best prayer after the obligatory is the night prayer' (Muslim 1163).

title: Speech — The Weight of Words
subtitle: Guarding the tongue without going silent
steps: The standard: 'whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent' (Bukhari 6018).
The backbite prohibition: 'would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You detest it!' (49:12).
The license for reconciliation: 'there is no ghibah in six: the one who openly sins, the one who commits injustice...' (Abu Dawud 4880) — naming injustice to stop it is not backbiting.
Argue gently: 'I guarantee a house at the edge of Paradise for the one who leaves an argument even when he is right' (Abu Dawud 4800).
Praise with honesty: 'the one who deceives us is not one of us' (Muslim 101).
The dua: Allahumma a'inni 'ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni 'ibadatik — 'O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You, and worship You well' (Abu Dawud 1522).
sources: Qur'an 49:12; Sahih al-Bukhari 6018; Sahih Muslim 101; Sunan Abi Dawud 4800, 4880

title: Greetings & Sneezing
subtitle: The salam as a transaction of peace
steps: Spread the salam: 'as-salamu 'alaykum' — to those you know and those you do not (Bukhari 12).
The return: wa 'alaykum as-salam — and the reward: 'you will not enter Paradise until you love one another; spread the salam among you' (Muslim 54).
Sneezing: the sneezer says Alhamdulillah; the hearer says Yarhamukallah; the sneezer returns: Yahdikumullah... (Bukhari 6224).
Yawning is from Shaytan — suppress it: 'yawning is from Shaytan, so if any of you yawns let him suppress it as much as he can' (Bukhari 6226).
The handshake completes the greeting: 'when two Muslims meet and shake hands, their sins fall away before they part' (Abu Dawud 5212, hasan).
Enter gatherings with the salam; leave with it — the salam begins and ends every sitting.

title: Hajj — The Fifth Pillar
subtitle: Who must go, when, and what it requires
steps: The obligation: 'And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to Allah by people who are able to undertake it' (3:97) — ability means provision, health, route safety, and the family's maintenance during absence.
The condition of islam: Hajj of a non-Muslim is not accepted; the Prophet ﷺ said: the non-Muslim's deeds are like a mirage (Muslim 2116 context).
Once in a lifetime — the Prophet ﷺ was asked if the newly performed Hajj was for every year: 'no; the Hajj is once; what exceeds that is voluntary' (Muslim 1337).
The timing: Hajj is in specific days of Dhul-Hijjah (2:197) — the 8th to the 13th; Umrah can be performed at any time of year.
Before departure: settle debts, write a will, seek forgiveness, leave the family's provision — Umar kept the emigrants' deposits in trust; a pilgrim's household is a trust too.
The reward: the accepted Hajj has no reward but Paradise — 'from one Hajj to another is expiation for what is between them' (Bukhari 1521).

title: Ihram — Entering the Sacred State
subtitle: Two cloths, two rak'ahs, one talbiyah
steps: The ghusl before ihram (sunnah), then perfume applied to the body before the niyyah — not after (Bukhari 1539).

Men: two seamless white cloths; no fitted garments, no head covering — 'the muhrim wears no turban, no hooded cloak, no trousers...' (Bukhari 134). Women wear ordinary modest dress; no face veil, no gloves (Bukhari 1838).
Pray two rak'ahs (the Prophet ﷺ prayed them at the miqat, Bukhari 1534), then state the niyyah: Labbaika Allahumma Hajjan (or 'Umratan) — and the umrah niyyah suffices until the Hajj days.
The talbiyah, raised aloud by men: Labbaika Allahu labbaik, labbaika la sharika laka labbaik... — the Prophet ﷺ said: Jibril instructed me to keep raising it (Muslim 1184).

What ihram forbids: sewn garments (men), head covering (men), face cover and gloves (women), cutting hair or nails, perfume, hunting, marriage contracts — 'the muhrim may not marry, nor be married' (Muslim 1409).
Violations are expiated by fidyah — fasting three days, feeding six poor people, or sacrificing a sheep (2:196); the schools detail which applies to which violation.
madhhabNote: Which violations require which expiation differs by school and cause (perfume vs shaving vs intimacy) — this is exactly the case for a Hajj seminar or a trusted fiqh manual, not a quick card.

title: Tawaf & Sa'i
subtitle: Seven circuits and seven lengths — the rites Hajar taught us
steps: Enter al-Masjid al-Haram with the right foot and the dua; approach the Black Stone — kiss it, touch it, or point to it with the raised hand and takbir: 'there is no harm' — that was the Prophet's ﷺ instruction to the crowd (Bukhari 1607).
Tawaf: seven circuits beginning and ending at the Stone, the Kaaba on your LEFT — counterclockwise; the first three rounds are ramal (brisk, chest out) for men in the arrival tawaf (Bukhari 1602).
Between circuits, at the Yemeni corner and the Stone: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah... (Bukhari 1615); two rak'ahs of tawaf behind the Maqam after completion (2:125).
Then sa'i: between Safa and Marwah seven lengths (Safa→Marwah = one), remembering Hajar's search — 'then she descended... and hurried as a person hurries in distress' (Bukhari 3364).
Men jog between the green-lit portion of the course (the valley where Hajar ran); the Prophet ﷺ said: the area between the two green markers is where the valley ran (Muslim 1211).

Completion of Umrah: the men shave (the Prophet ﷺ prayed for the shavers thrice and the short-cutters once, Bukhari 1727) or shorten; women cut a fingertip's length — 'do not shave; women shave not' (Abu Dawud 1984).

title: The Day of Arafah
subtitle: The day the religion was perfected
steps: Stand at Arafat — the Prophet ﷺ said: the Hajj is Arafat; whoever reaches Arafat before dawn has caught the Hajj (Tirmidhi 889).
The timing: presence within the boundaries from noon until sunset; departure after sunset is sunnah (most scholars).
The dua of the day: the Prophet ﷺ said the best dua is the dua of Arafah — La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (Tirmidhi 3585).
The forgiveness: 'there is no day on which Allah frees more people from the Fire than the day of Arafah' (Muslim 1348).
For the non-pilgrim: fasting Arafah expiates the year before and the year after — for those not on Hajj (Muslim 1162).
The perfection: on this day, at Arafat, the verse descended: 'This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you' (5:3).

title: Fasting — The Fourth Pillar
subtitle: From dawn to sunset, and what breaks the fast
steps: The obligation: 'O believers, fasting is prescribed for you as it was for those before you' (2:183) — Ramadan by sighting the moon: 'fast when you see it and break when you see it' (Bukhari 1909).
The niyyah is settled each night before dawn — the Prophet ﷺ said: whoever does not intend the fast before Fajr has no fast (Nasa'i 2331).
What breaks it: eating, drinking, and marital relations (2:187); the Prophet ﷺ listed the one who eats forgetting and continues — 'it is Allah who fed him and gave him drink' (Bukhari 1933).
What does not: tasting food without swallowing (with need), the siwak, rinsing the mouth, nose drops (the majority), eye drops — the Prophet ﷺ used kohl while fasting (Abu Dawud 2380).
The exemptions with make-up: illness and travel — 'whoever is ill or on a journey, a number of other days' (2:184); the pregnant and nursing feed a poor person per day (fidyah) per the majority.
The night is for eating: 'take the pre-dawn meal, for in the suhoor there is blessing' (Bukhari 1923).
madhhabNote: The details of make-up vs fidyah for the elderly, pregnancy, and chronic illness differ by school — consult a local mufti for your case.

title: Ramadan Nights
subtitle: Taraweeh, the khatm, and Laylat al-Qadr
steps: The prayer: the Prophet ﷺ led the companions in congregation for several nights, then discontinued, saying: 'I feared it would be made obligatory for you' (Bukhari 1129).

Umar established the congregational taraweeh with twenty rak'ahs — 'what an excellent innovation this is' (Bukhari 2010 narration context); eight or twenty are both practiced among the pious predecessors.
The pace: the Prophet ﷺ used to recite in Ramadan — Surah ad-Dukhan took a portion of the night (Bukhari 4996); aim for recitation you can sustain thirty nights.

Laylat al-Qadr: better than a thousand months (97:3) — in the odd nights of the last ten; Aisha asked what to say if she found it: Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibbul-'afwa fa'fu 'anni (Tirmidhi 3513).
The i'tikaf: seclusion in the mosque for the last ten — the Prophet ﷺ never abandoned it in the last ten years (Bukhari 2024).
The generosity: the Prophet ﷺ was more generous in Ramadan than the free wind (Bukhari 6).
madhhabNote: Taraweeh length (8 vs 20 rak'ahs) is a difference of practice among the schools and the salaf — both are sound; follow your local congregation without argument.

title: Istikhara — The Guidance Prayer
subtitle: Two rak'ahs and the dua of surrender
steps: The need: 'when one of you intends a matter, let him pray two rak'ahs other than the obligatory, then say...' — the full istikhara dua taught by the Prophet ﷺ (Bukhari 6382).

The dua's heart: 'O Allah, I ask Your guidance by Your knowledge, and power by Your might... If this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and my outcome, decree it for me and ease it; and if it is evil, turn it away from me and turn me from it, and decree good for me wherever it is' (Bukhari 6382).
Then act: istikhara is not a demand for a vision; the scholars said: 'seek the means, then act on what settles in the heart after the dua.'

The answer's forms: ease and opening (a sign to proceed), difficulty and closed doors (a sign to withdraw), or continued neutrality — in which case repeat up to seven days, then choose (per many scholars).
What it is not: a substitute for due diligence, consultation, or fiqh — 'the one who consults does not regret' (Tabarani, hasan).
What it is: the admission that outcomes belong to Allah — the worshipper asks to be steered, then walks with tawakkul.

title: Tawba — The Return
subtitle: Four conditions the scholars agreed upon
steps: The conditions: (1) abandon the sin now; (2) regret it sincerely; (3) resolve not to return; (4) restore the right if it was a violation of another's right — their property, their honor, or their due (Muslim 1551's framework in the tradition).
The door's hours: 'Allah accepts the servant's repentance until the soul reaches the throat' (Tirmidhi 3537) — and the Prophet ﷺ added: until the sun rises from the west.
The replacement promise: 'except those who repent, believe, and do righteousness — Allah will replace their evil deeds with good ones' (25:68-70).
For the habitual sinner: 'the one who repents from sin is as if he had no sin' (Ibn Majah 4250); repeat the return without despair — the previous card in this library is Shaytan's despair-play.
The concealment: 'conceal the sin of your brother and Allah will conceal yours' — do not publicize past sins even in confession beyond need (Baihaqi).
The seal: the Prophet ﷺ taught: 'by the One in whose hand is my soul, if you did not sin, Allah would replace you with people who sin and seek forgiveness, and He would forgive them' (Muslim 2749).

title: Earning — Halal Livelihood
subtitle: The body built from the unlawful will not enter Paradise
steps: The principle: 'Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure' (Muslim 1015) — 'the truthful merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs' (Tirmidhi 1209).
The prohibition core: 'Allah has cursed the one who consumes interest and the one who pays it' (Muslim 1598) — the contract is the sin, not only the receipt.
The scales: full measure — 'woe to the fraudsters... who take full measure when they receive but diminish when they give' (83:1-3); give the customer his due even when he does not check.
The honest broker: 'the two parties of a transaction have the option as long as they have not parted; if they were truthful and clear, their transaction is blessed' (Bukhari 2079).
The laborer: 'give the worker his wages before his sweat dries' (Ibn Majah 2443).
The doubtful: 'leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not' (Tirmidhi 2518).
sources: Qur'an 83:1-3; Sahih al-Bukhari 2079; Sahih Muslim 1015, 1598; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1209, 2518

title: Marriage — The Nikah
subtitle: Half the religion, in a contract of mercy
steps: The command frame: 'marry the spouseless among you' (24:32); 'when the servant marries, he has completed half of his religion' (Baihaqi, hasan).
The core condition: consent — the virgin is not married without her permission, and her silence is her permission (Bukhari 6946).
The sermon: the Prophet ﷺ addressed marriages with praise of Allah and the dua for barakah — 'and the best of you is the best of you to their wives' (Tirmidhi 3895).
The witnesses: 'there is no marriage except with a wali and two witnesses of good character' (Abu Dawud 2085, graded hasan-sahih).
The mahr: 'the most blessed mahr is the easiest' (Abu Dawud 2117) — a right owed, never a purchase.
The spirit: 'the believers are but brothers' (49:10) begins at home — the Prophet ﷺ said the best of you is the best to his family, and he was the best to his (Tirmidhi 3895).
sources: Qur'an 24:32; 49:10; Sahih al-Bukhari 6946; Sunan Abi Dawud 2085, 2117; Sunan at-Tirmidhi 3895

title: Illness & Patience
subtitle: The fever as expiation, the visit as worship
steps: The expiation: 'no fatigue, nor illness, nor anxiety, nor sorrow, nor harm befalls a Muslim except that Allah expiates by it — even the thorn' (Bukhari 5641).
The dua: 'O Allah, Lord of mankind, remove the harm and heal; You are the Healer' — said over the sick seven times (Bukhari 5675).
The patience ranks: 'amazing is the affair of the believer... if harm reaches him he is patient, and that is good for him' (Muslim 2999).
Visiting the sick: 'a Muslim has five rights over his brother: returning the salam, visiting the sick, attending the funeral, accepting invitations, and blessing the sneezer' (Muslim 2162).
The reminder: illness is a visitor with a purpose — the Prophet ﷺ visited a sick Bedouin who had no believer in his tent and sat with him until the man's heart softened (Bukhari 5654).
The worst moment: 'seek healing, servants of Allah, for Allah has not created an illness except He created its healing' (Bukhari 5676).

title: Gratitude — Shukr
subtitle: The wealth that increases
steps: The root: 'if you are grateful, I will surely increase you' (14:7) — gratitude as the economics of the soul.
The tongue: say Alhamdulillah at every event, Alhamdulillah after every meal, Alhamdulillah 'alaa kulli hal — in ease and hardship (the Prophet's ﷺ practice in all states).
The heart: recognize the gift as a gift — the scholars called shukr 'the heart's acknowledgment of the blessing's source.'
The limbs: 'show gratitude to Allah' means worship — the prayer at the moment of blessing, the charity at the moment of increase.
The hardship form: 'whoever is not grateful for little will not be grateful for much' — and the patient one in hardship receives reward without measure (Ibn Majah 4212).
The completion: gratitude is the key to retention — blessings flee the ungrateful the way water flees a cracked vessel (Abu Dawud, hasan).
sources: Qur'an 14:7; Sunan Ibn Majah 4212; Sunan Abi Dawud 4843

title: Travel — The Wayfarer's Adab
subtitle: Provision, safety, and the dua of the road
steps: The intention: travel is worship's cousin — 'traveling through the land is [an act of] obedience' (34:18 context); intend remembrance and halal purpose.
The companionship: 'the best companions are four, and the best expeditions are four hundred' (Abu Dawud 2628) — travel with the God-fearing.
The boarding dua: Bismillah, Allahu Akbar (3x) — the Prophet ﷺ said: then Allah says: you are protected (Abu Dawud 2602).
The tawakkul form: 'Allahumma hawwin 'alayna safarana...' — the travel dua of the Prophet ﷺ (Muslim 1342).

The shortened prayer (qasr): four-rak'ah prayers are prayed two — 'there is no blame upon you in shortening the prayer if you fear' (4:101); most scholars add: while traveling beyond the city's edge, under conditions.
The return: repeat the boarding dua and add: ayibuna, ta'ibuna, 'abiduna, lirabbina hamidun — returning, repenting, worshipping, praising our Lord (Muslim 1343).
sources: Qur'an 4:101; Sahih Muslim 1342-1343; Sunan Abi Dawud 2602, 2628
madhhabNote: Qasr's distance and duration limits differ by school (the majority: ~85km and under ~15 days) — follow your school's fiqh for your journey.

title: The Morning & Evening Adhkar
subtitle: The fortress that takes seven minutes
steps: The time: morning — after Fajr until sunrise; evening — after Asr until Maghrib (per most scholars).
Ayat al-Kursi (once each) — 'whoever recites it in the morning and evening is protected until he recites it again' (Nasa'i).
The three quls: al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, an-Nas — three times each, blown into the hands and wiped over the body (Abu Dawud 5082).
The master dua: 'We have entered the morning (evening), and the kingdom belongs to Allah; the praise belongs to Allah...' (Muslim 2723).
Sayyid al-istighfar — the best form of seeking forgiveness, morning and evening (Bukhari 6306).
Protection scope: 'these suffice you against everything' — the Prophet ﷺ said of the mu'awwidhat for every harm (Abu Dawud 5082).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6306; Sahih Muslim 2723; Sunan Abi Dawud 5082

title: The New Baby — Welcome Rites
subtitle: Adhan in the ear, tahnik, and the aqiqah
steps: The adhan: the Prophet ﷺ said the adhan in the ear of al-Hasan when he was born (Abu Dawud 5105) — the first sound a Muslim child hears.
The name: choose a good name — 'you will be called on the Day of Resurrection by your names and your fathers' names' (Abu Dawud 4948); the Prophet ﷺ named on the seventh day.
The tahnik: chew a date and rub the child's palate with it — the Prophet ﷺ did this for Abdullah ibn Zubayr and prayed for him (Bukhari 5467).
The aqiqah: two sheep for a boy, one for a girl — 'for the boy two equivalent sheep, and for the girl one' (Tirmidhi 1513); on the seventh day.
The shaving: the child's head is shaved and silver equal to the hair's weight given in sadaqah (Tirmidhi 1513).
The dua for the parents: 'may Allah make him blessed for you and make his footsteps firm upon the religion' — the Prophet's ﷺ wording for the newborn (Bukhari 5472 context).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 5467, 5472; Sunan Abi Dawud 5105; Sunan at-Tirmidhi 1513

title: The Rights of Parents
subtitle: Paradise's gate is at their feet
steps: The command's weight: 'your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and goodness to parents' — joined to tawhid itself (17:23).
The smallest word: never say so much as 'uff' to them (17:23); the Prophet ﷺ called the uff the lightest of what is forbidden (Bukhari 5975).
The lowered wing: 'lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and say: My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small' (17:24).
The order of service: the mother first, thrice over — 'who is most deserving of my good companionship? Your mother, then your mother, then your mother, then your father' (Bukhari 5971).
After their passing: pray for them, give charity on their behalf, honor their friends — 'the finest of your fathers are the best of them' (Muslim 2552).
The duty's limit: obedience in goodness only — 'no obedience to any created being in disobedience to the Creator' (Ahmad 1095).

title: The Rights of Neighbors
subtitle: Forty neighbors — and the one who does not harm them
steps: The measure: 'by Allah, he does not believe; by Allah, he does not believe' — the companions asked: who, O Messenger of Allah? He said: the one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm (Bukhari 6016).
The scope: the neighbor's right extends to forty houses in every direction (Tirmidhi 1919).
The Quran's own neighbors: 'worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor and the far neighbor' (4:36).
The practical form: share food, visit in illness, attend their funerals, shelter their good name — 'whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor' (Bukhari 6018).
The harm list: no smoke, no noise, no litter, no prying eyes over the fence — the Prophet ﷺ said: 'he does not enter Paradise whose neighbor is not safe from his harm.'
The test: the Prophet ﷺ was asked about a neighbor who harms: 'keep enduring his harm and seek Allah's help' — until, the scholars add, harm becomes unbearable, then seek counsel.

title: Oaths & Vows
subtitle: Swearing is a mortgage on the tongue
steps: The default: do not swear by other than Allah — 'whoever swears by other than Allah has committed shirk' (Tirmidhi 1535).
The caution: 'do not swear a lot in your buying and selling; it removes the blessing' (Bukhari 2087).
The inadvertent oath: feeding or clothing ten poor people, freeing a slave, or fasting three days — 'so its expiation is the feeding of ten poor people' (5:89).
The deliberate broken oath: same kaffarah — and Allah said: 'so protect your oaths' (5:89).

The vow (nadhr): the Prophet ﷺ said: 'it does not bring the son of Adam anything I decreed for him or turn away anything I decreed against; it only extracts from the miser' (Bukhari 6608) — yet once made, it must be kept.
The mercy: 'the expiation for a vow is its kaffarah' — and the scholars teach: if the vow's object becomes impossible or sinful, the vow dissolves by intention's failure, per school details.

title: Witr & The Night Routine
subtitle: Closing the day the way it opened — with light
steps: The standing practice: the Prophet ﷺ never abandoned the witr, neither traveling nor resident — 'make the witr your last prayer at night' (Bukhari 990).
The qunut — the schools differ on its place: Hanafi: before ruku' in witr nightly; Shafi'i: in the second half of Ramadan; Hanbali: may be before or after; the evidence supports all.
The dua al-qunut wording the Prophet ﷺ taught (for the one who wishes to memorize): Allahumma-hdini fiman hadayt... (Nasai 1745).
The sleep-with-worship balance: if you fear missing Fajr, pray witr and sleep; the Prophet ﷺ said: 'there are no two witr in one night' (Abu Dawud 1438).
The ending: the last words before sleep — Subhan Allah, walhamdulillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wallahu akbar (Bukhari 6306).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 990, 6306; Sunan an-Nasa'i 1745; Sunan Abi Dawud 1438
madhhabNote: Witr's timing (before or after sleep) and qunut's placement differ by school — all from the Prophet's ﷺ practice on different nights; follow one school consistently.

title: Seeking Knowledge
subtitle: The path walked slowly, with humility
steps: The intention: the Prophet ﷺ said: 'whoever seeks knowledge to compete, or to be praised, or to draw attention — his destination is the Fire' (Tirmidhi 2654).
The humility equipment: 'whoever travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise' (Muslim 2699).
The manners before the teacher: sit where you are placed, do not argue, do not say 'but so-and-so said' — the salaf called the student's humility half the knowledge.
The pace: 'knowledge is by learning' — and the tradition adds: take from the mouths of the trustworthy, verify, and write.
The application test: 'knowledge is a shield; acting without knowledge is deviation' (Daraqutni) — the first knowledge to act on: prayer and its times.
The chain's honor: 'the scholars are the inheritors of the prophets' (Abu Dawud 3641).
sources: Sahih Muslim 2699; Sunan Abi Dawud 3641; Sunan at-Tirmidhi 2654

title: Hardship & Relief
subtitle: The dua of distress — the treasury of the tested
steps: The distress dua: 'La ilaha illa Allah, al-'azim, al-halim. La ilaha illa Allah, Rabbul-'arshil-'azim...' — the Prophet ﷺ said: no servant supplicates with it concerning anything except that Allah answers him (Bukhari 6346).
The anxious heart: 'Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-hammi wal-hazan...' — the Prophet ﷺ taught it to Abu Umamah, and his anxiety left him (Abu Dawud 1551).
The debt: 'Allahumma akfini bihalalika 'an haramika...' — 'O Allah, suffice me with Your halal against Your haram, and enrich me by Your bounty from all besides You' (Tirmidhi 3565).
The grief response: 'there is no deity but Allah, the Great, the Clement; there is no deity but Allah, Lord of the magnificent Throne...' — recited upon every distress (Bukhari 6326).
The patience anchor: 'amazing is the affair of the believer — all of it is good for him' (Muslim 2999).
The exit guarantee: 'whoever leaves a thing for Allah, Allah will give him something better' (Ahmad).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6326, 6346; Sunan Abi Dawud 1551; Sunan at-Tirmidhi 3565

title: Preparing — The Practical Will
subtitle: Five duties every believer owes the future
steps: Write the will: 'it is prescribed for you, when death approaches any of you, if he leaves wealth, to make a bequest...' (2:180) — the Prophet ﷺ said: a Muslim should not pass two nights without his will written (Tirmidhi 2103), except he who has no bequestable property.
The debt ledger: record every debt, every trust, every unresolved claim — the martyr's sins are forgiven but his debts are settled first (Muslim 1886).
Teach your heirs the dua of the dying — 'whoever's last words are la ilaha illa Allah enters Paradise' (Abu Dawud 3116): practice saying it now, slowly, until it is the easiest sentence you own.
The funeral instructions: leave word for a simple janazah, no wailing, swift burial — 'hasten with the deceased' (Bukhari 1315).

The continuing charity: establish one sadaqah jariyah before death — a well, a tree, a student's tuition — the three things that keep paying: ongoing charity, useful knowledge, a righteous child (Muslim 4222).

The gentle end: keep the family reconciled — the Prophet ﷺ said: 'the doors of the Garden are opened on Mondays and Thursdays, and every servant who does not associate anything with Allah is forgiven except the two who are estranged' (Tirmidhi 3100).
sources: Qur'an 2:180; Sahih al-Bukhari 1315; Sahih Muslim 1886, 4222; Sunan at-Tirmidhi 2103, 3100

title: Hajj — The Fifth Pillar (Walkthrough)
subtitle: The full journey, day by day, from ihram to the farewell tawaf
steps: Enter ihram at the miqat (or before it for air travelers): ghusl, the two white cloths, the niyyah and talbiyah — Labbaika Allahumma Hajjan.
Day 1 (8 Dhul-Hijjah, Yawm at-Tarwiyah): enter ihram for Hajj if not already; proceed to Mina and pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha and Fajr there, shortened but not combined.
Day 2 (9 Dhul-Hijjah, Arafah): stand at Arafat from noon until sunset — the essence of Hajj. Combine Dhuhr and Asr at Zuhr time, shortened. Pray, make dua, remember; no fasting for the pilgrim.
After sunset, leave for Muzdalifah without praying Maghrib at Arafat: pray Maghrib and Isha combined at Isha time; spend the night (or part of it, especially for the weak and women).

Day 3 (10 Dhul-Hijjah, Yawm an-Nahr): stone Jamrat al-Aqabah with seven pebbles; sacrifice; shave or shorten the hair (taqsir/halq) — the first release from ihram; then the tawaf al-ifadah and sa'i of Hajj, completing the release.
The days of Tashreeq (11-13): stone the three jamarat daily after noon, seven each — or leave after two days, the concession for those who hasten (2:203).
Farewell: before departing Makkah, the tawaf al-wada' — one final circuit. The menstruating woman is excused from it (Bukhari 1755).
madhhabNote: Stoning order details, Muzdalifah stay length, and combining prayers differ in detail between schools — follow your group's mutawwif (guide) or your school's fiqh.

title: Umrah — In a Day
subtitle: The smaller pilgrimage, complete from ihram to release
steps: Enter ihram at the miqat: ghusl, the cloths, niyyah for Umrah, talbiyah — Labbaika Allahumma Umrah.

Arrive al-Masjid al-Haram with the talbiyah still on your tongue; begin tawaf at the Black Stone (kiss, touch, or point with takbir), seven circuits, the Kaaba on your left, ramal (brisk) in the first three if others are present.
Pray two rak'ahs of tawaf behind the Maqam Ibrahim if possible; drink Zamzam.
Sa'i: Safa to Marwah seven lengths, remembering Hajar's run; men jog between the green lights.
Exit ihram: shave (preferred) or shorten the hair — the Umrah is complete. Men shorten from all sides; women cut a fingertip's length only.
No raml in sa'i after the first tawaf; no visit to the rawdah is required but is beloved if time allows.
madhhabNote: Women do not ramal and do not shave; touching the Black Stone is sunnah, never an obligation — the crowd's safety comes first.

title: The Day of Arafah — Even at Home
subtitle: The 9th of Dhul-Hijjah for the pilgrim and the one far away
steps: For the pilgrim: stand within the boundary of Arafat from noon to sunset — standing even a moment within it completes the pillar; combine Dhuhr and Asr at Zuhr time, two by two.
Fill the hours with dua — the best is the taught one: La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (Tirmidhi 3585).
Do not fast on Arafah if you are the pilgrim standing there — the day is for drinking and remembering (the pilgrims' exemption: Bukhari 1661).
For everyone else: FAST this day — it expiates the year before and the year after (Muslim 1162); say the takbir and the shahada abundantly.
After sunset, depart for Muzdalifah — but not before the sun sets; the impatient crowds cannot move the sun.
The one who misses the standing entirely has missed that Hajj and owes a makeup with a sacrifice (Bukhari 1560) — so the boundary signs matter; follow the guides.
madhhabNote: Saying 'standing' means presence within Arafat's bounds, not a specific posture or location upon the mountain — the day is mercy, not ordeal.

title: Ihram — Entering the Sacred State
subtitle: The wardrobe, the words, and the boundaries before the House
steps: Ghusl (full wash), then perfume on the BODY before the niyyah — never on the cloths after (Bukhari 1539).
Men: two seamless white cloths, no fitted garment, no head cover. Women: ordinary modest dress; no face veil, no gloves (Bukhari 1838).
Pray two rak'ahs at the miqat, then declare: Labbaika Allahumma Hajjan (or Umrah); raise the talbiyah aloud: Labbaika Allahumma labbaik...

What ihram forbids: sewn garments (men), head cover (men), face cover and gloves (women), cutting hair or nails, perfume, hunting, marriage contracts — 'the muhrim may not marry, nor be married' (Muslim 1409).
Violations carry fidyah — fasting three days, feeding six poor persons, or sacrificing a sheep (2:196); the schools assign which expiation to which violation — ask your guide.
The talbiyah continues until the stoning of Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 10th — let your tongue not fall silent while your heart is present.
madhhabNote: Which violations require which expiation (perfume vs shaving vs intimacy) differs by school and cause — this is precisely the case for a Hajj seminar or a trusted manual.
